comment: The NuGet packages the tree builds against. A version is either a minimum or exactly one version in brackets. Of a minimum, such as 1.4.0, the restore takes the newest version of the same major version on the same channel: a stable minimum admits stable versions only, a prerelease one the prereleases whose label begins with the same word (2.5.4-experimental admits 2.6.0-experimental3, not 2.6.4); the major version is raised only by editing the minimum. A version in brackets, such as [1.4.0], holds the package at exactly that version, and the update leaves it there: a satellite of the release (Win2D, WebView2, CppWinRT) moves on its own, and a newer one can need a Windows App SDK component newer than the release has, which stops the restore in the check of the referenced components of Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK.Runtime (VerifyReferencedWindowsAppSdkComponentVersions); such a package is held until the release moves. A hold is a stopgap until a release that satisfies the satellite exists: the tree follows the newest versions of its channel, and the usual answer to a satellite that needs a newer component is to move the release forward with the update. No package is held now. The versions taken are those tools/packages.lock.json records; a newer one comes only with the update, tools\build.ps1 -UpdatePackages, which writes that file anew to be committed. cmake/wxl_packages.cmake reads this file at configure: every package becomes a PackageReference item of its helper MSBuild project, whose restore writes what it resolved into tools/packages.lock.json and the configure into the list <build>/wxl.packages/restored-packages.json, which winui-srcgen and wxl.gen.ui read their packages from. Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK is the umbrella package of the Windows App SDK release the tree builds against, and its dependencies are the packages of that release. The release is an experimental one: the profile full projects types that the WinUI of the stable releases 2.5.1 and 2.6.4 does not declare (WrapPanel, LayoutPanel, FlowLayout, PagerControl and the ink controls). Microsoft.Windows.CppWinRT carries cppwinrt.exe and the MSBuild targets that build the C++/WinRT projection of the Windows SDK and of the packages.
